raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The serial chest X-rays demonstrate progressive, diffuse bilateral fluffy infiltrates and nodular opacities rather than a solitary nodule or localized consolidation. This radiographic pattern is characteristic of the diffuse pneumonic or multinodular subtype of bronchioloalveolar carcinoma (now adenocarcinoma in situ/minimally invasive adenocarcinoma), which indicates widespread disease and typically carries a poorer prognosis compared to localized forms.
